title: Complete packet analysis and synthesis
domain: Vector spaces over a field
hypotheses: Let $P_1,\ldots,P_m\in\operatorname{End}(X)$ satisfy $P_aP_b=\delta_{ab}P_a$ and $\sum_aP_a=I_X$. Set $X_a=P_aX$.
statement_tex:
The maps
\[
 \mathcal A x=(P_ax)_a,\qquad
 \mathcal S(x_a)_a=\sum_ax_a
\]
are inverse isomorphisms between $X$ and $\bigoplus_aX_a$. In particular,
$x=\sum_aP_ax$ uniquely.
interpretation: The archived source proves coordinate and ℓ2 projector specializations; the SG result is for arbitrary complete algebraic projectors.

title: Transfer algebra and packet paths
domain: The packet space of SG-01
hypotheses: Let $S,T\in\operatorname{End}(X)$. Set $T_{ba}=P_bTP_a$, viewed as a map $X_a\to X_b$.
statement_tex:
\[
 T=\sum_{a,b}P_bTP_a,\qquad
 (ST)_{ca}=\sum_bS_{cb}T_{ba}.
\]
The block representation is an algebra isomorphism to
$\operatorname{End}(\bigoplus_aX_a)$, with multiplication by contraction of
intermediate packets. For every integer $k\ge1$, iterating the product gives
\[
 P_{a_k}T^kP_{a_0}
 =\sum_{a_1,\ldots,a_{k-1}}
 (P_{a_k}TP_{a_{k-1}})\cdots(P_{a_1}TP_{a_0}).
\]
interpretation: Composition is proved for finite Laurent filter-bank operators; arbitrary packet transfer paths remain a prose theorem.

title: Refinement preserves represented operators
domain: Finite complete packet systems
hypotheses: Let $(Q_\rho)$ refine $(P_a)$, with a partition of fine labels into $F_a$ and $P_a=\sum_{\rho\in F_a}Q_\rho$.
statement_tex:
\[
 P_bTP_a=\sum_{\sigma\in F_b}\sum_{\rho\in F_a}Q_\sigma TQ_\rho.
\]
The coordinate changes $J=\mathcal A_Q\mathcal S_P$ and
$C=\mathcal A_P\mathcal S_Q$ satisfy $CJ=I$ and $JC=I$ on their packet
coordinate spaces. Refinement is exact before any child packet is discarded.
interpretation: The source proves supplied coordinate refinement and its bounded ℓ2 specialization, not every abstract packet operator refinement.

title: Pulled-back transform packets
domain: Vector spaces with an invertible transform
hypotheses: Let $V:X\to Y$ be an isomorphism and $(E_a)$ a finite complete packet family on $Y$.
statement_tex:
The operators $P_a=V^{-1}E_aV$ are a complete packet family on $X$.
For a unitary $V$ and orthogonal coordinate selectors $E_a$ in a Hilbert space,
\[
 \|x\|^2=\sum_a\|P_ax\|^2.
\]
interpretation: A bijective coordinate reindexing is a particular isometric transform; the arbitrary invertible-transform conjugation theorem is not a recovered target.

title: Polyphase analysis and convolution kernels
domain: Absolutely summable sequences on $\mathbb Z$
hypotheses: Fix an integer $N\ge1$. Let $h,x\in\ell^1(\mathbb Z)$ and $y=h*x$. Define $x_a[q]=x[Nq+a]$ and $y_b[q]=y[Nq+b]$, for $0\le a,b<N$.
statement_tex:
Interleaving the $N$ channels recovers $x$ exactly. With
\[
 h_{ba}[k]=h[Nk+b-a],
\]
the output channels satisfy
\[
 y_b[q]=\sum_{a=0}^{N-1}\sum_{t\in\mathbb Z}h_{ba}[q-t]x_a[t].
\]
Thus convolution becomes an $N\times N$ transfer-kernel system.
interpretation: Exact integer round trips and finite-support convolution are formalized. The SG claim allows ℓ1 infinite-support kernels and needs its absolute-convergence argument.

title: The arithmetic of residual alias ambiguity
domain: Unit-modulus exponential nodes
hypotheses: Let $z\in\mathbb C$, $|z|=1$, and suppose $u=z^N$ and $w_j=z^{r_j}$ are known, with $N\ge1$ and integer offsets $r_j$. Let $d=\gcd(N,r_1,\ldots,r_k)$.
statement_tex:
Exactly $d$ unit-modulus nodes satisfy the same data. Hence the physical node
is unique precisely when $d=1$. If integers $c,b_1,\ldots,b_k$ obey
$Nc+\sum_jr_jb_j=d$, then
\[
 u^c\prod_jw_j^{b_j}=z^d.
\]
For $d=1$ this is an explicit exact de-aliasing formula.
interpretation: Unit-circle power observations, finite alias group, and Bézout/gcd identification.

title: Measurement and decomposition obstructions
domain: An arbitrary measurement model and linear packet classes
hypotheses: Let $M:X\to Y$ be any map and let an edge assignment $J:X\to\mathcal J$ be specified. Separately, let $\mathcal S,\mathcal J$ be linear subspaces of a common vector space.
statement_tex:
If $Mf_0=Mf_1$ but $J(f_0)\ne J(f_1)$, no map $R:Y\to\mathcal J$ recovers
the correct edge for both. If $\mathcal S\cap\mathcal J\ne\{0\}$, the
sum decomposition $f=s+j$ is not unique. In particular, finitely many point
samples on a periodic interval cannot recover every arbitrary interval packet.
interpretation: Measurement-fiber identifiability and direct-sum uniqueness in the declared model.

title: No uniform location stability without separation
domain: Two-jump periodic packets of fixed known amplitudes
hypotheses: Fix a finite set $F\subset\mathbb Z$ of derivative-moment indices. For $0<\delta<\pi/4$, compare locations $(0,\delta)$ and $(\pi,\pi+\delta)$, both with amplitudes $(1,-1)$.
statement_tex:
Their unordered location sets have permutation-matched bottleneck distance at
least $\pi-\delta$, while their measured derivative moments satisfy
\[
 |m_n-\widetilde m_n|
 =|(1-e^{-in\pi})(1-e^{-in\delta})|
 \le2|n|\delta\qquad(n\in F).
\]
There is no Lipschitz inverse for locations with one constant on all distinct
two-jump configurations, even at this fixed order and with known amplitudes.
interpretation: Matched circular location metric and the fixed-order narrow-pulse counterexample.

title: Out-of-band matched identification
domain: Periodic integrable signals with one known edge shape
hypotheses: Let $\mathcal S_K$ be the trigonometric polynomials of degree at most $K$. Let $m\in L^1(\mathbb T)$ and a finite nonempty set $F\subset\{n:|n|>K\}$ satisfy $D_F=\sum_{n\in F}|\widehat m(n)|^2>0$.
statement_tex:
On $X=\mathcal S_K+\operatorname{span}\{m\}$, the functional
\[
 \ell_F(g)=D_F^{-1}\sum_{n\in F}\overline{\widehat m(n)}\widehat g(n)
\]
satisfies $\ell_F(s+am)=a$. The decomposition is direct. If the measured
coefficients have errors $\eta_n$, then
\[
 |\widetilde a-a|\le D_F^{-1/2}\Bigl(\sum_{n\in F}|\eta_n|^2\Bigr)^{1/2}.
\]
interpretation: The formal supplied-edge cancellation is related; Fourier out-of-band identification of an unknown scalar coefficient is additional.

title: The singularity-exact block operator
domain: The model space of SG-09
hypotheses: Let $P_Jg=\ell_F(g)m$, $P_S=I-P_J$, and let $S_M$ be Fourier truncation of degree $M\ge K$.
statement_tex:
\[
 P_J^2=P_J,\quad P_S^2=P_S,\quad P_SP_J=P_JP_S=0,
 \quad P_S+P_J=I_X,
\]
and the resolved reconstruction obeys
\[
 \mathcal R_M=S_MP_S+P_J=I_X.
\]
interpretation: Supplied-edge error cancellation is formal. The Fourier-defined block, its projector identities and exactness on the model class are separate prose obligations.

title: Resolved error for an analytic background
domain: Periodic signals with a supplied exact edge packet
hypotheses: Let $f=s+j$ with $|\widehat s(n)|\le Ce^{-\rho|n|}$, where $C\ge0$ and $\rho>0$. Use the canonical uniformly convergent Fourier-series representative of $s$. Set $\mathcal R_Mf=S_Ms+j$.
statement_tex:
The reconstruction error is exactly $f-\mathcal R_Mf=s-S_Ms$, and
\[
 \|f-\mathcal R_Mf\|_\infty
 \le\frac{2Ce^{-\rho(M+1)}}{1-e^{-\rho}}.
\]
The bound is uniform across the jumps of $j$.
interpretation: The cancellation part is formal; analytic Fourier decay, tail summation and the concrete signal-norm instantiation are not targets here.

title: The scaled interval-edge Gibbs profile
domain: The interval packet $j=\mathbf1_{[-a,a)}$ on $\mathbb T$
hypotheses: Assume $0<a<\pi$, let $\lambda_M=M+1/2$, and use the right edge coordinate $x_M(z)=a-z/\lambda_M$.
statement_tex:
Uniformly for $z$ in compact real intervals,
\[
 S_Mj(x_M(z))\longrightarrow\frac12+\frac1\pi\operatorname{Si}(z),
 \qquad \operatorname{Si}(z)=\int_0^z\frac{\sin t}{t}\,dt.
\]
The first positive maximum of the limiting profile is $1+G$, where
\[
 G=\frac{\operatorname{Si}(\pi)}\pi-\frac12
   =0.089489872236\ldots.
\]
interpretation: Dirichlet-kernel scaled limit, sine-integral profile, and the local Gibbs overshoot.

title: Positive Fourier averaging preserves range
domain: Periodic bounded real signals
hypotheses: Let $\sigma_M=(M+1)^{-1}\sum_{k=0}^MS_k$ be the Fejer mean. Suppose $0\le j\le1$ almost everywhere.
statement_tex:
Then $0\le\sigma_Mj\le1$ everywhere. For an interval packet, this suppresses
overshoot while retaining a continuous transition rather than an exact jump.
interpretation: Fejér-kernel positivity, integral normalization, and range preservation almost everywhere.

title: Residualized sparse injectivity
domain: Finite real or complex Euclidean spaces
hypotheses: Let $\mathcal S\subseteq\mathbb F^m$ be a subspace, $P$ its orthogonal projector, $R=I-P$, $D\in\mathbb F^{m\times d}$, and $A=RD$. Let $s\ge0$ be an integer.
statement_tex:
Every vector $\alpha$ with $\|\alpha\|_0\le s$ is uniquely determined by
$A\alpha$ if and only if
\[
 \ker A\cap\{h:\|h\|_0\le\min(2s,d)\}=\{0\}.
\]
Equivalently every set of at most $\min(2s,d)$ columns is independent.
With the convention $\operatorname{spark}(A)=d+1$ when all $d$ columns are
independent, the equivalent condition is
$\operatorname{spark}(A)>\min(2s,d)$.
For $s=0$ uniqueness is automatic.
interpretation: Projected sparse null-secant injectivity and the capped spark convention.

title: Sparse noise stability and support thresholding
domain: The Euclidean model of SG-14
hypotheses: Assume $s\ge1$, $d\ge1$, and the injectivity condition of SG-14. Let $y=s_0+D\alpha_0+\eta$, $s_0\in\mathcal S$, $\|\alpha_0\|_0\le s$, and $\|R\eta\|_2\le\epsilon$. Let $\widehat\alpha$ be $s$-sparse with $\|A\widehat\alpha-Ry\|_2\le\epsilon$.
statement_tex:
Define
\[
 \gamma=\min_{\substack{\|h\|_2=1\\\|h\|_0\le\min(2s,d)}}\|Ah\|_2>0.
\]
Then
\[
 \|\widehat\alpha-\alpha_0\|_2\le2\epsilon/\gamma,
 \qquad\|D(\widehat\alpha-\alpha_0)\|_2
 \le2\|D\|_2\epsilon/\gamma.
\]
If every nonzero true coefficient has magnitude greater than $4\epsilon/\gamma$,
thresholding at $2\epsilon/\gamma$ with a strict greater-than rule recovers
the true support.
interpretation: Restricted column separation, nuisance projection contraction, and sparse support bounds.

title: Profiled one-packet discovery and its finite gap
domain: Finite real dictionaries with positive amplitudes
hypotheses: Let $B$ have full column rank, $P$ be the orthogonal projector onto its range, $R=I-P$, and let $\mathcal Q$ be a finite mask library with $Rq\ne0$ for every $q$. Suppose $y=B\theta_*+a_*q_*$, with $a_*>0$ and $q_*\in\mathcal Q$.
statement_tex:
For an unrestricted scalar amplitude the least-squares profile is
\[
 \widehat a(q)=\frac{\langle Rq,Ry\rangle}{\|Rq\|_2^2},
 \qquad J(q)=\|Ry-\widehat a(q)Rq\|_2^2.
\]
The true mask has $\widehat a(q_*)=a_*$ and $J(q_*)=0$.
It is the unique zero-residual positive-amplitude mask exactly when no other
residualized mask lies on its positive ray. Define the closed rays
$C_q=\{aRq:a\ge0\}$. If
\[
 \Gamma=\inf_{q\ne q_*}\operatorname{dist}(Ry,C_q)>0,
\]
with the convention $\inf\varnothing=+\infty$, then every perturbed residualized datum $Ry+e$ with $\|e\|_2<\Gamma/2$
selects $q_*$ uniquely by nearest-ray distance.
interpretation: Finite objective gap and stability are formal under a strict optimum and uniform objective errors; profiled dictionary identification and its particular score are additional.

title: Mask error is a support geometry calculation
domain: Finite binary masks
hypotheses: Let $q,\widetilde q\in\{0,1\}^m$ and $a,\widetilde a\in\mathbb R$.
statement_tex:
\begin{align*}
 \|aq-\widetilde a\widetilde q\|_2^2
 &=|a-\widetilde a|^2|\operatorname{supp}q\cap\operatorname{supp}\widetilde q|\\
 &\quad+|a|^2|\operatorname{supp}q\setminus\operatorname{supp}\widetilde q|
 +|\widetilde a|^2|\operatorname{supp}\widetilde q\setminus\operatorname{supp}q|.
\end{align*}
For $a=\widetilde a=1$ the squared norm is the cardinality of the symmetric
support difference.
interpretation: The source provides extended measurable-mask identities and bounds; the SG mixed-amplitude finite-vector identity is a distinct specialization/derivation.

title: Differentiation isolates an exponential moment packet
domain: The class $\mathcal U_{K,L}$
hypotheses: Use the Fourier convention in Section 1. Let $n>K$ and $z_\ell=e^{-i\tau_\ell}$.
statement_tex:
\[
 Dj=\sum_\ell a_\ell\delta_{\tau_\ell},\qquad
 m_n:=2\pi in\widehat f(n)=\sum_{\ell=1}^ra_\ell z_\ell^n.
\]
For a non-bandlimited integrable background the same formula holds with
an additive defect $e_n=2\pi in\widehat s(n)$.
interpretation: Continuous distributional derivative and Fourier normalization to exponential moments.

title: Hankel rank detects the actual order
domain: Finite exponential moments over $\mathbb C$
hypotheses: Let $m_{n_0+k}=\sum_{\ell=1}^r c_\ell z_\ell^k$, with distinct nonzero nodes and nonzero coefficients. Let $H_{h,w}=(m_{n_0+i+j})_{0\le i<h,\ 0\le j<w}$, with $h,w\ge r$.
statement_tex:
Writing $V_h=(z_\ell^i)_{i,\ell}$ and $V_w=(z_\ell^j)_{j,\ell}$,
\[
 H_{h,w}=V_h\operatorname{diag}(c_\ell)V_w^{\mathsf T},
 \qquad\operatorname{rank}H_{h,w}=r.
\]
For $r=0$ the Hankel matrix is zero. The transpose is algebraic and is not
a conjugate transpose.
interpretation: Hankel/Vandermonde factorization, rank, and zero-order interpretation.

title: Exact Prony annihilation and location recovery
domain: The nonzero-order moment model of SG-19
hypotheses: Assume $r\ge1$ and $2r$ consecutive moments $m_{n_0},\ldots,m_{n_0+2r-1}$ are known.
statement_tex:
The unique monic annihilator
\[
 Q(z)=\prod_{\ell=1}^r(z-z_\ell)=\sum_{k=0}^{r-1}q_kz^k+z^r
\]
is recovered from
\[
 H_{r,r}q=-v,\qquad v=(m_{n_0+r+i})_{i=0}^{r-1}.
\]
Its roots are exactly the nodes. Once the nodes are known, $r$ consecutive
moments determine the coefficients uniquely by a Vandermonde solve.
For unit-modulus nodes the corresponding locations are
$\tau_\ell=-\arg z_\ell\pmod{2\pi}$.
interpretation: Prony annihilator uniqueness, polynomial roots, and matched location recovery.

title: Canonical periodic integration of jump data
domain: A period of length $T>0$
hypotheses: Let distinct locations $\tau_\ell\in\mathbb R/(T\mathbb Z)$ and real amplitudes $a_\ell$ satisfy $\sum_\ell a_\ell=0$. Define the mean-zero periodic sawtooth $G_T(x)=1/2-x/T$ for $0<x<T$, with the right-continuous endpoint value.
statement_tex:
\[
 j(x)=\sum_\ell a_\ell G_T(x-\tau_\ell)
\]
is the unique mean-zero right-continuous piecewise-constant packet with those
jumps. Its distributional derivative is $\sum_\ell a_\ell\delta_{\tau_\ell}$.
interpretation: Canonical mean-zero periodic primitive and its representative.

title: Finite exact unknown-order reconstruction
domain: The real class $\mathcal U_{K,L}$
hypotheses: Let $K\ge0$ and $L\ge1$ be known integers. Assume exact Fourier coefficients for $-K\le n\le K$ and $K+1\le n\le K+2L$.
statement_tex:
Those data uniquely determine the actual active order $r$, every jump
location and amplitude up to permutation, the canonical edge packet $j$,
the smooth coefficients of $s$, and the complete signal $f$ as an $L^1$ class
and as its selected right-continuous representative. The high-frequency
budget is $2L$ complex coefficients. The low budget is $2K+1$ coefficients,
with conjugate symmetry redundancy for a real signal.
interpretation: Finite exact data budget, unknown/zero order branch, and synthesis modulo representative.

title: Hankel perturbation from Fourier noise
domain: A rectangular Hankel matrix of derivative moments
hypotheses: Let measured Fourier coefficients have errors $\eta_n$ and moment errors $\epsilon_n=2\pi in\eta_n$. Let $E=(\epsilon_{n_0+i+j})$ have $h\ge1$ rows and $w\ge1$ columns.
statement_tex:
\[
 \|E\|_2\le\|E\|_F
 \le\sqrt{hw}\max_{0\le i<h,\ 0\le j<w}|\epsilon_{n_0+i+j}|.
\]
In particular, an error bound $|\eta_n|\le\eta$ implies
\[
 \|E\|_2\le2\pi\sqrt{hw}\eta\max_{i,j}|n_0+i+j|.
\]
interpretation: Fourier-noise scaling and the rectangular Hankel Frobenius/spectral bound.

title: Annihilator coefficient perturbation
domain: The invertible square Prony system of SG-20
hypotheses: Write $Hq=-v$, and suppose $\widetilde H=H+E$, $\widetilde v=v+e$. Assume $\|H^{-1}\|_2\|E\|_2<1$.
statement_tex:
The perturbed system is invertible, and its solution satisfies
\[
 \|\widetilde q-q\|_2
 \le\frac{\|H^{-1}\|_2}{1-\|H^{-1}\|_2\|E\|_2}
       (\|e\|_2+\|E\|_2\|q\|_2).
\]
interpretation: Perturbed inverse/Neumann gate and annihilator coefficient error.

title: Conditional simple-root disk localization
domain: Monic complex polynomials of the same degree
hypotheses: Let $r\ge1$ and $Q(z)=\prod_{\ell=1}^r(z-z_\ell)$ have distinct roots and $\widetilde Q=Q+E_Q$. Choose $0<\rho<\tfrac12\min_{\ell\ne k}|z_\ell-z_k|$ when $r\ge2$, or any $\rho>0$ when $r=1$.
statement_tex:
If for every $\ell$
\[
 \sup_{|z-z_\ell|=\rho}|E_Q(z)|
 <\min_{|z-z_\ell|=\rho}|Q(z)|,
\]
then $\widetilde Q$ has exactly one root, counted with multiplicity, in each
disk $|z-z_\ell|<\rho$. All its roots are thereby matched with error less
than $\rho$. A sufficient explicit bound on each circle is
\[
 \sum_{k=0}^{r-1}|\widetilde q_k-q_k|(|z_\ell|+\rho)^k
 <\rho\prod_{j\ne\ell}(|z_\ell-z_j|-\rho).
\]
interpretation: Strict Rouché disk gate, one root per disk, and conditional true-root matching.

title: Amplitude stability with perturbed nodes
domain: A square or overdetermined Vandermonde amplitude fit
hypotheses: Let $V$ have full column rank, $m=Va$, $\widetilde V=V+\Delta V$, and $\widetilde m=m+e$. Assume $\sigma_{\min}(V)>\|\Delta V\|_2$. Let $\widehat a$ minimize $\|\widetilde Vb-\widetilde m\|_2$.
statement_tex:
\[
 \|\widehat a-a\|_2
 \le\frac{\|e\|_2+\|\Delta V\|_2\|a\|_2}
 {\sigma_{\min}(V)-\|\Delta V\|_2}.
\]
For unit nodes in rows with nonnegative powers $n$, matched chord error
$|\widehat z_\ell-z_\ell|\le\delta$ gives the entry bound
$|\widehat z_\ell^n-z_\ell^n|\le n\delta$.
interpretation: Perturbed full-column-rank least squares and amplitude stability.

title: Shared-node offset channels
domain: Derivative moments with an additive defect
hypotheses: Fix integers $N\ge2$, $q_0\ge1$, and an offset $r\ge0$. Suppose $m_n=\sum_\ell a_\ell z_\ell^n+e_n$, with $|z_\ell|=1$.
statement_tex:
\[
 m_{(q_0+q)N+r}=\sum_\ell b_{\ell,r}u_\ell^q+e_{(q_0+q)N+r},
 \quad u_\ell=z_\ell^N,\quad b_{\ell,r}=a_\ell u_\ell^{q_0}z_\ell^r.
\]
For each matched edge $b_{\ell,r+1}=z_\ell b_{\ell,r}$.
If $|\widehat s(n)|\le C_s(1+|n|)^{-p-2}$ with $p\ge0$, then for
nonnegative $q,r$
\[
 |e_{(q_0+q)N+r}|\le2\pi C_s(q_0N)^{-p-1}.
\]
interpretation: Defective moment model and shared aliased exponential nodes across offsets.

title: Order recovery with a supplied singular threshold
domain: Finite rectangular complex matrices
hypotheses: Let $H=H_0+E$, with $H_0$ of rank $r\ge1$, $k=\min(h,w)\ge r$, and $\epsilon=\|E\|_2<\sigma_r(H_0)/2$. Supply a threshold $t$ with $\epsilon<t<\sigma_r(H_0)-\epsilon$.
statement_tex:
Exactly $r$ singular values of $H$ exceed $t$. If $r=0$, a supplied
threshold $t>\|E\|_2$ selects zero. If $r=k$, all $k$ singular values exceed
the threshold and no nonexistent $\sigma_{k+1}$ is used.
interpretation: Complex singular-value perturbation and a supplied threshold, including full rank.

title: Exact phase from adjacent offset products
domain: One matched unit-circle coefficient progression
hypotheses: Let $R\ge1$ be an integer counting adjacent products, and let $c_r=bz^r$ for $0\le r\le R$, with $b\ne0$ and $|z|=1$. Define $S(c)=\sum_{r=0}^{R-1}\overline{c_r}c_{r+1}$.
statement_tex:
\[
 S(c)=R|b|^2z\ne0,\qquad\Phi(c):=S(c)/|S(c)|=z.
\]
Two channels already give $z=c_1/c_0$ exactly. More channels provide repeated
adjacent relations, without an unconditional deterministic averaging gain.
interpretation: Adjacent offset products with R≥1 and nonzero amplitude.

title: Deterministic offset-phase perturbation
domain: A noisy progression as in SG-29
hypotheses: Let $c_r=bz^r+e_r$ for $0\le r\le R$, with $R\ge1$, $b\ne0$, $|z|=1$, and $|e_r|\le\epsilon$. Put $A=R|b|^2$ and $\Delta=R(2|b|\epsilon+\epsilon^2)$. Assume $\Delta<A$.
statement_tex:
The phase sum is nonzero and
\[
 |\Phi(c)-z|\le\frac{2\Delta}{A}
 =\frac{4\epsilon}{|b|}+2\left(\frac\epsilon{|b|}\right)^2.
\]
interpretation: Offset phase denominator and explicit defect-to-phase bound.

title: A zero offset residual tests a progression
domain: Finite complex offset data
hypotheses: Let $R\ge1$, $c_0\ne0$, and $|\zeta|=1$. Define $\nu(c,\zeta)=\bigl(\sum_{r=0}^{R-1}|c_{r+1}-\zeta c_r|^2\bigr)^{1/2}/\bigl(\sum_{r=0}^{R-1}|c_r|^2\bigr)^{1/2}$.
statement_tex:
Then $\nu(c,\zeta)=0$ if and only if $c_r=c_0\zeta^r$ for
$0\le r\le R$.
interpretation: Normalized residual zero exactly characterizes a finite progression.

title: Unique branch selection under a strict margin
domain: Nth roots of a unit-modulus estimate
hypotheses: Let $N\ge2$, $|z|=1$, $u=z^N$, and $\overline u=\widehat u/|\widehat u|$ with $\widehat u\ne0$. Let $\rho$ be a root of $\overline u$ continuously associated with $z$, and $\widetilde z$ a coarse phase estimate.
statement_tex:
If
\[
 |\widetilde z-z|+|\rho-z|<\sin(\pi/N),
\]
then $\rho$ is the unique root of $\overline u$ nearest to $\widetilde z$.
It equals the branch an oracle chooses by the true-node neighborhood.
interpretation: The finite strict-margin selection principle is formal; circular Nth-root geometry, associated-root error and the particular metric gate remain additional.

title: Associated roots divide the angular error
domain: Unit-modulus nodes and their associated root branches
hypotheses: Let $N\ge1$, $z^N=u$, $|z|=|u|=|\overline u|=1$, and $|\overline u-u|\le\eta<2$. Let $\rho$ be the associated root along the shortest angular perturbation.
statement_tex:
\[
 |\rho-z|\le2\sin\left(\frac1N\arcsin\frac\eta2\right)
 \le\frac2N\arcsin\frac\eta2.
\]
For a nonzero raw estimate, $|\widehat u-u|\le\epsilon$ implies
$|\widehat u/|\widehat u|-u|\le2\epsilon$. Thus when the raw error tends to
zero, correct lifting gains a factor $1/N$ in chord and angular accuracy.
interpretation: Associated root branch and divided angular perturbation.

title: An explicit exact self-calibration budget
domain: Bandlimited background with a bounded number of jumps
hypotheses: Let $f\in\mathcal U_{K,L_{\max}}$, with $L_{\max}\ge1$. Supply $N\ge2$, $q_0\ge1$ with $q_0N>K$, and assume the active aliased nodes $u_\ell=z_\ell^N$ are distinct.
statement_tex:
The Fourier coefficients at the high indices
\[
 \mathcal I_0=\{(q_0+q)N:0\le q\le2L_{\max}\},\qquad
 \mathcal I_1=\{(q_0+q)N+1:0\le q<L_{\max}\}
\]
determine the unknown edge order, every physical node, and every jump amplitude
exactly. The high-frequency budget is $3L_{\max}+1$. Low modes
$-K\le n\le K$ then give the complete signal. No supplied jump neighborhood
is required.
interpretation: Explicit exact calibration data budget and distinct active alias nodes.

title: Conditional asymptotic rates after calibrated lifting
domain: A selected sequence of decimation scales
hypotheses: Let $p\ge0$, fix $q_0$ and the finite number of channel samples and offsets, and take a sequence $N\to\infty$. Assume distinct aliased nodes, uniform rank-threshold gaps/local inverse bounds for the aligned Prony and coefficient fits, $|b_{\ell,0}|\ge b_{\min}>0$, uniformly bounded amplitudes, and the strict branch margin of SG-32. Suppose the moment defect is $O(N^{-p-1})$.
statement_tex:
The threshold-selected order is eventually correct. The aligned lifted nodes
and locations satisfy
\[
 |\widehat z_\ell-z_\ell|=O(N^{-p-2}),\qquad
 d_{\mathbb T}(\widehat\tau_\ell,\tau_\ell)=O(N^{-p-2}).
\]
The recovered amplitudes satisfy
$|\widehat a_\ell-a_\ell|=O(N^{-p-1})$.
interpretation: Uniform inverse bounds, coefficient lower bounds, strict branch margin, and conditional rates.

title: Resolved synthesis splits the two error sources
domain: A normed signal space
hypotheses: Let $f=s+j$, let $\widehat j$ belong to the same space, and let $A_M$ be a bounded linear operator with norm at most $C_M$. Define $\widehat f_M=A_M(f-\widehat j)+\widehat j$.
statement_tex:
\[
 f-\widehat f_M=(s-A_Ms)+(I-A_M)(j-\widehat j),
\]
and therefore
\[
 \|f-\widehat f_M\|\le\|s-A_Ms\|+(1+C_M)\|j-\widehat j\|.
\]
If $\widehat j=j$, the complete error equals the smooth approximation error.
interpretation: The additive error split is formal; the A_M linearity rewrite and its operator-norm amplification are not this source type.

title: Sharp additive L1 control for normalized jump packets
domain: Mean-zero periodic packets of period $T>0$
hypotheses: Let $j,\widehat j$ have matched real jump data $(a_\ell,\tau_\ell)$ and $(\widehat a_\ell,\widehat\tau_\ell)$, with both amplitude sums zero. Use their canonical representatives and let $d_\ell=d_T(\tau_\ell,\widehat\tau_\ell)\le T/2$.
statement_tex:
\[
 \|j-\widehat j\|_1
 \le\frac T4\sum_\ell|a_\ell-\widehat a_\ell|
 +2\sum_\ell|\widehat a_\ell|d_\ell(1-d_\ell/T).
\]
In particular the simpler location term $2\sum_\ell|\widehat a_\ell|d_\ell$
is valid. The printed location coefficient one in the inherited
self-calibration manuscript is not valid for mean-zero normalization.
interpretation: Measurable-mask error infrastructure is related, but the corrected mean-zero periodic sawtooth calculation and sharp factor two are not formalized here.

title: A conditional global L1 reconstruction rate
domain: The rate family of SG-35 with $T=2\pi$
hypotheses: Assume a fixed finite jump count, bounded jump amplitudes, the hypotheses of SG-35, and a bounded linear smooth reconstruction $A_M$ acting on $L^1(\mathbb T)$. Require $\widehat j$ to be the canonical packet of real matched estimated amplitudes whose sum is zero. Let $b_M=\|s-A_Ms\|_1$ and $C_M=\|A_M\|_{L^1\to L^1}$.
statement_tex:
\[
 \|j-\widehat j\|_1=O(N^{-p-1}),\qquad
 \|f-\widehat f_M\|_1\le b_M+O((1+C_M)N^{-p-1}).
\]
For Fourier truncation, $C_M=O(1+\log(M+1))$. If also
$|\widehat s(n)|\le C_s(1+|n|)^{-p-2}$, its smooth remainder satisfies
$b_M=O(M^{-p-1})$. Taking $M$ comparable to $N$ yields
$O((1+\log N)N^{-p-1})$.
interpretation: Supplied-error combination is related; calibrated parameter rates, canonical jump L1 control and Fourier operator-norm growth remain prose obligations.

title: Shared-location multichannel recovery
domain: A finite collection of exponential moment channels
hypotheses: Let $m_n^{(c)}=\sum_{\ell=1}^ra_{c\ell}z_\ell^n$, with distinct common unit-modulus nodes. At each node at least one channel amplitude is nonzero. Form the stacked linear recurrence system for a monic polynomial of degree $r$ and assume its coefficient matrix has column rank $r$.
statement_tex:
The stacked system uniquely recovers the common annihilator
$Q(z)=\prod_\ell(z-z_\ell)$. Its roots recover the common locations.
With $r$ consecutive moments per channel, a channelwise Vandermonde solve
recovers every amplitude, including amplitudes that vanish in that channel.
interpretation: Stacked full-column-rank recurrence, common annihilator, and channelwise Vandermonde recovery.

title: Confluent annihilation and the leading offset phase
domain: Polynomial-exponential sequences
hypotheses: Let $m_n=\sum_{\ell=1}^rz_\ell^nP_\ell(n)$ with distinct nonzero nodes and $\deg P_\ell\le d$. Let $E$ be the forward shift. For an offset ratio assume $N\ge1$ and the leading coefficient of $P_\ell$ at degree $d$ is nonzero.
statement_tex:
\[
 \prod_{\ell=1}^r(E-z_\ell)^{d+1}m=0.
\]
For offset $v\ge0$, writing a decimated channel as
\[
 m_{(q_0+q)N+v}=\sum_\ell u_\ell^q
                   \sum_{h=0}^d\gamma_{\ell,v,h}q^h,
 \qquad u_\ell=z_\ell^N,
\]
the highest-degree coefficients satisfy
$\gamma_{\ell,1,d}/\gamma_{\ell,0,d}=z_\ell$.
This ratio applies to separated, matched confluent terms with nonzero leading
coefficient. The displayed annihilator is not asserted to have minimal order
when leading coefficients vanish.
interpretation: Confluent shift annihilation, polynomial degree, and nonvanishing leading offset coefficients.

title: Model mismatch enters the same sparse stability bound
domain: A finite-dimensional background-edge model
hypotheses: Use $A=RD$ from SG-14 and assume $s\ge1$, $d\ge1$, and its restricted constant $\gamma>0$. Suppose $y=s_0+D\alpha_0+e+\eta$, with $s_0\in\mathcal S$, $\|\alpha_0\|_0\le s$, and $\|R(e+\eta)\|_2\le\epsilon$. Let $\widehat\alpha$ be $s$-sparse with $\|A\widehat\alpha-Ry\|_2\le\epsilon$.
statement_tex:
\[
 \|\widehat\alpha-\alpha_0\|_2\le2\epsilon/\gamma.
\]
If an actual edge $j$ obeys $\|j-D\alpha_0\|_2\le\delta$, then
\[
 \|j-D\widehat\alpha\|_2\le\delta+2\|D\|_2\epsilon/\gamma.
\]
The theorem applies to finite image dictionaries under these printed
sparsity, residual, and restricted-injectivity hypotheses.
interpretation: Restricted sparse injectivity with projected model mismatch and edge approximation error.

title: Ideal nested-span refitting decreases residual
domain: A Hilbert space with finite selected packet spans
hypotheses: Let $V_1\subseteq V_2\subseteq\cdots$ be finite-dimensional subspaces. Let $P_k$ be the orthogonal projector onto $V_k$.
statement_tex:
\[
 \|f-P_{k+1}f\|\le\|f-P_kf\|,
 \qquad f-P_kf\perp V_k.
\]
If $\bigcup_kV_k$ is dense, then $P_kf\to f$ in norm.
interpretation: The source proves density and orthogonality for particular ℓ2 coordinate packets; arbitrary nested finite-span projector convergence is not a recovered target.

title: Ridge refitting has a different stationarity law
domain: Finite-dimensional real packet designs
hypotheses: Let $M\in\mathbb R^{m\times d}$, $y\in\mathbb R^m$, and $\lambda>0$. Let $c$ minimize $\|y-Mc\|_2^2+\lambda\|c\|_2^2$ and set $r=y-Mc$.
statement_tex:
The minimizer is unique and
\[
 (M^{\mathsf T}M+\lambda I)c=M^{\mathsf T}y,
 \qquad M^{\mathsf T}r=\lambda c.
\]
Adding candidate columns cannot increase the minimized ridge objective,
but exact orthogonality $M^{\mathsf T}r=0$ is not the ridge stationarity law.
Even a complete pixel basis need not give zero residual when $\lambda>0$.
interpretation: Positive ridge normal equations, uniqueness, and modified residual stationarity.

title: Clipping is nonexpansive toward a bounded truth
domain: Real pixel arrays with Euclidean norms
hypotheses: Define $C(x)$ coordinatewise by $C(t)=\min(1,\max(0,t))$. Suppose the truth $f$ has every coordinate in $[0,1]$.
statement_tex:
\[
 \|C(x)-C(y)\|_2\le\|x-y\|_2,\qquad
 \|C(x)-f\|_2\le\|x-f\|_2.
\]
Clipping is nonlinear; it is not the bounded linear synthesis operator in
SG-36. Its truth-error guarantee depends on the stated box constraint.
interpretation: Scalar clipping nonexpansiveness, box truth assumption, and Euclidean assembly.

title: An exact residual archive preserves the object
domain: Any normed signal space
hypotheses: Let an approximation $q$ to an available object $f$ be supplied, and retain the complete residual $r=f-q$.
statement_tex:
The synthesis $q+r=f$ is exact. This identity supplies no sparsity, compression,
or recovery-from-fewer-measurements conclusion. In finite pixel space the
full pixel basis likewise spans every image in the ideal unregularized model.
interpretation: Exact full residual identity and ideal finite pixel spanning; no compression inference.

title: Bounded identities extend from a dense core
domain: Normed spaces and bounded linear maps
hypotheses: Let $D$ be a dense linear subspace of $X$, and let $A,B:X\to Y$ be bounded linear operators agreeing on $D$.
statement_tex:
Then $A=B$ on $X$. Consequently a finite packet identity established on a
dense core extends to a completion when both represented operators have
bounded extensions. An infinite projector sum additionally requires a
specified convergent synthesis; bounded finite identities alone do not
supply that convergence.
interpretation: An explicit dense core and bounded finite projector identity are formal examples; the general bounded-operator extension theorem is not a recovered target.
